title: bug: QA's landed gate exits the whole QA wrapper (worktree_stop → exit 1) on a row-level miss such as no recorded completion commit, so every landed-gate park permanently costs a QA seat until a human relaunches it: qa-7328a40d on 7cef0861 (11-03 22:44Z) and qa-58a8e460 on 87cba58c (11-04 05:25Z) (both launchers)
description:
Seen twice. The seat is lost each time:
- 2026-11-03 22:44:34Z: qa-7328a40d's pre-flight on task-7cef0861 printed MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND "no recorded completion commit" and report_blocked the row. At 22:44:35Z the #general system line says "qa-7328a40d left (unexpected_exit:1)".
- 2026-11-04 05:25:21Z: qa-58a8e460 on task-87cba58c, same code. At 05:25:21.925Z: "qa-58a8e460 left (unexpected_exit:1)", and its .moe/workers record is DEAD.
After the second loss the board was down to 2 QA seats with 7 REVIEW rows queued.

Cause:
- qa_landed_gate (scripts/moe-agent.sh:7068, called at :11005) routes every miss through worktree_stop (:3227).
- worktree_stop prints the code, sends one report_blocked, stops the sidecar and runs `exit 1`. The EXIT trap then deregisters the seat.
- The ps1 twin does the same: Assert-MoeQaLandedCommit (moe-agent.ps1:6536, called at :10244) goes through Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat (:3115).
- worktree_stop was written for worker provisioning guards (git too old, the control checkout not on moe/control, a path too long). Those are seat-level conditions that would recur on every iteration, so stopping the seat is right there.
- "This task has no recorded completion commit" is a fact about one row. The report_blocked has already parked that row (a non-resource block by the assignee frees the seat), so the next claim would pick a different REVIEW row. Exiting only removes review capacity, with no human told to relaunch.

Expected:
- For a row-level miss, at least the no-recorded-completion case, the QA pre-flight parks the row with its one report_blocked, launches no CLI, and goes back to the loop top for a fresh pre-flight and claim, as after any other ended session. The seat stays registered.
- Keep stopping the seat for seat-level failures, such as a control HEAD that cannot be read. Classify the other branches (completion not a commit; completion not in the control HEAD after a successful follow), and document the split.
- Placement: scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} are shared with open rows on other functions: cc4213c0 (REVIEW, the sh VM-route outage), 561d347c (PLANNING, wt_publish's journal), 62ec51f1 and d861f3de (the ps1 VM route). That needs no edge in worktree mode. Put the new harness arm in its own block, and edit both twins with a TOOL-witnessed editor, then run bash -n / ParseFile.
definitionOfDone: In both launchers, a QA pre-flight whose task has no recorded completion commit report_blocks that row once, launches no CLI, and continues to a fresh pre-flight instead of exiting. A harness arm (postflight-worktree.cjs or the worktree landing harness) shows the same seat claiming and starting a second REVIEW row after the park. The arm fails on today's wrappers.

A seat-level failure (for example an unreadable control HEAD) still stops the seat as today. The split between the gate's branches is stated in scripts/CLAUDE.md (the qa_landed_gate sentence under Control follow) and in the design doc's QA-gate text.
parity-check.{sh,ps1} passes, bash -n and the ps1 ParseFile check pass, and the existing postflight-worktree and worktree-landing arms stay green.

implementationPlan.description:
sh wrapper (DoD 1, 2), the scripts/moe-agent.sh hunks of code.diff. Edit in place in W with the Edit tool (in a task worktree the atomic-save rule does not apply), then `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`. Leave worktree_stop untouched: every worker provisioning guard uses it.
(a) qa_control_preflight.
- Set the global `QA_LAND_B=""` first, then: `if sync_land_target "$target"; then QA_LAND_B="$LAND_B"; elif [ "$LAND_WT_PUB" = remote ]; then <the existing WARN line>; fi`, then follow_control_checkout.
- In local mode sync_land_target only reads refs/heads/<target> (no fetch), so QA_LAND_B is the local tip read BEFORE the follow. In remote mode it is origin's tip, just fetched.
- Extend the header comment.
(b) New `qa_gate_park DETAIL` right after it. It sends one moe_rpc report_blocked with {taskId, workerId, reason: "MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND: DETAIL", blockedOnTaskIds: []}.
- Why the explicit []: an omitted list makes report_blocked parse task ids out of the reason. If they are all DONE, it answers dependenciesSatisfied and does NOT block, so the row would stay claimable and the seat would re-claim it forever (mem:gotcha-report-blocked-reason-ids-become-blockers).
- On success it prints `[WARN] MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND: DETAIL` and `[WARN] task <tid> is parked with no CLI run; this seat goes on to its next claim.`, then returns 0.
- Error handling: when the args build or the RPC fails, it prints `[ERROR] MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND: DETAIL` and worktree_stop's `[WARN] moe.report_blocked failed for <tid>; the seat stops anyway.`, runs stop_heartbeat_sidecar, then exit 1. There is no second call, so a row the daemon never parked is never re-claimed in a loop.
(c) qa_landed_gate.
- The python takes "$tid" as argv[1]. It prints nothing unless the context's task.id equals it; it prints the sha when it is 40 lowercase hex, else 'none'.
- Empty → worktree_stop "task $tid: the pre-flight get_context did not answer for this task, so its recorded completion is unknown". This is seat-level, as today.
- 'none' → qa_gate_park <today's no-recorded-completion detail> and `return 1`.
- Unreadable HEAD → unchanged.
- Then a `why` variable:
  - cat-file -e fails → why = <today's not-a-commit detail>;
  - otherwise `merge-base --is-ancestor` rc != 0 → why = <today's not-in-HEAD detail>, and rc != 1 (a git error) → worktree_stop "$why".
- With why set:
  - QA_LAND_B non-empty and (== HEAD, or `merge-base --is-ancestor "$QA_LAND_B" "$head"` exits 0) → qa_gate_park "$why"; return 1;
  - else worktree_stop "$why". HEAD lacks the synced tip (a failed sync or follow), which every row would hit, so the seat stops.
- Keep every detail string byte-identical to today's, so the existing reason regexes still match. Rewrite the header comment to state the split.
(d) Call site, the WT-13 (§6.4) block: `qa_landed_gate || continue`, with a 2-line comment.
- The continue also skips the loop-end --no-loop break; the precedent is `account_wait_recheck || continue`.
- FIRST_RUN=false was already set, so the next pass gets the poll sleep like any ended session.
- The gate runs before the baseline, the live marker, the account lease and the heartbeat sidecar, so nothing needs undoing.
- report_blocked's hand-back closes the QA claim's attempt (taskStore closeAttemptsOnHandBack).
- Green check: the sh leg with MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-qa-gate,wt-qa-park → 2 ok.

implementationPlan.description:
ps1 twin (DoD 1, 2), the scripts/moe-agent.ps1 hunks of code.diff, ported with the Edit tool. Keep the UTF-8 BOM, then ParseFile must report 0 errors. Leave Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat untouched.
(a) Invoke-MoeQaControlPreflight.
- Set `$script:MoeQaLandB = ''` first.
- When Get-MoeGitTop answers:
  - `$remote = -not (Test-MoeNoRemote $git.Top)`;
  - `$L = @{ Remote = $remote; B = ''; Msg = '' }`;
  - `$script:MoeQaLandB = [string](Sync-MoeLandTarget $git.Top $target $res $L)`. Use the RETURN value: it is '' on any failure, even when $L.B was set (diverged).
- Print the existing WARN only when `$remote -and -not $script:MoeQaLandB`.
- Then Invoke-MoeControlFollow.
(b) New `Invoke-MoeQaGatePark([string]$Detail)` before Assert-MoeQaLandedCommit.
- Inside try/catch: Invoke-MoeRpc report_blocked @{ taskId = $preflightTaskId; workerId = $WorkerId; reason = "MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_BEHIND: $Detail"; blockedOnTaskIds = @() }. PS 5.1 serializes @() as [], and the harness asserts it.
- Non-null reply → the same two [WARN] lines, `$script:MoeQaGateParked = $true`, return.
- Error handling: a null reply or a throw → the [ERROR] line, '[WARN] moe.report_blocked failed for <tid>; the seat stops anyway.', Stop-HeartbeatSidecar, exit 1.
(c) Assert-MoeQaLandedCommit, the same split.
- `$task = Get-MoeProp $Context 'task'; $id = Get-MoeProp $task 'id'; if (-not ($id -is [string] -and $id -ceq $TaskId))` → Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat with the no-context detail. Use the -is [string] guard because an array on the left of -cne filters instead of comparing.
- Bad sha → Invoke-MoeQaGatePark <detail>; return, with nothing on the pipeline.
- Not a commit, or not an ancestor → $why. `$rc -ne 1` → Stop.
- `$b = [string]$script:MoeQaLandB; if ($b -and ($b -ceq $head -or (Invoke-MoeGit ... 'merge-base','--is-ancestor',$b,$head).Rc -eq 0))` → park and return; else Stop.
- Passing returns the dynamic-context string as today. Use the same detail strings as sh.
(d) Call site:
```
$qaReview = Assert-MoeQaLandedCommit $preflightContext $preflightTaskId
if ($script:MoeQaGateParked) { continue }
$dynamicContext += $qaReview
```
(e) Loop top: `$script:MoeQaGateParked = $false` right after the in-loop `$script:AccountRelaunch = $false` (the 'Read once, just above' block, about :9540).
(f) The do-while condition (about :11672) gains `-or $script:MoeQaGateParked`, and the comment above it is extended. PowerShell's continue in a do-while jumps to the condition, so without this a -NoLoop run ends after the park; mutant m5 proved it.
- Green check: the ps1 leg via Windows node.exe, with WSLENV=MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY, MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-qa-gate,wt-qa-park and the fixture parent on /mnt/d → 2 ok.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. A 'park' flag on worktree_stop / Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat. Rejected: about 10 worker guards share them, and their output order and semantics would change.
2. Park every miss. Rejected: a control checkout that failed to fetch or follow misses every REVIEW row, so one seat would park the whole queue row by row. That is why a C miss is row-level only while HEAD holds the synced target tip (QA_LAND_B).
3. A new code such as MOE_QA_NO_COMPLETION. Rejected: it adds contract and docs churn, and the DoD keeps the code.
4. Checking report_blocked's taskStatus/seatFreed in the reply. Unnecessary: blockedOnTaskIds [] removes the only success-without-block path for a REVIEW row (dependenciesSatisfied), and the fake would need the real reply shape.
5. A second task id in the fake for the 'second REVIEW row'. Rejected: attempts, context and claims are hard-wired to task-postflight. FAKE_CTX_LANDING_FROM_CLAIM models the next row instead.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Loop mechanics:
- sh: the main loop is `{ while ...; done; tail; exit; }`. A `continue` skips the loop-end `--no-loop` break, so a park re-runs pre-flight even single-shot, as the account relaunch does.
- ps1: the loop is a do-while. `continue` jumps to the condition, hence the $script:MoeQaGateParked flag, reset at the loop top.
- FIRST_RUN/$firstRun are already false before pre-flight, so the next pass gets the poll sleep.
Daemon side:
- report_blocked by the assignee frees the seat (IDLE).
- updateTask's closeAttemptsOnHandBack closes the QA attempt, so no orphan attempt is left.
Harness:
- launch() keeps .moe/claim-count and second-claim across runs on one fixture.
- The single-shot taskless wait defaults to 300 s, over the 180 s launch LIMIT.
